Los Angeles Trade-Technical College · Credit for Prior Learning

139 approved courses, and the credit recommendation each one needs

LATTC has decided these courses can be awarded for military training. MAP needs a credit recommendation before an articulation can exist. Pick one per course — the recommendations are ranked, and the evidence behind each is one click away if you want it.

On 111 of the 139, LATTC's own veterans already hold the recommendation — the credit is sitting in their records with nothing to apply it to. Those bullets carry a ◆ LATTC students hold this chip.

How a recommendation is scored

Confidence is a ranking heuristic, not a probability, and it is built from three things you can see on every bullet — so you can disagree with the arithmetic rather than with a number.

✓ Peer precedent — 25%

A named California college has already attached this recommendation to a named course of their own. A fact, and the strongest thing in the mix.

⚙ Word fit — 55%

How well the recommendation's wording matches the course title. Each bullet names the word it matched on, so a weak match is obvious at a glance.

How widely it is held — 15%

How many California colleges' students already carry this recommendation. A recommendation on one exhibit at two colleges is a thinner bet than one on 31.

Hours against units — the cut

A recommendation is written in hours; a course is measured in units, and across 3,419 peer articulations that record both, 81% match exactly. So: more than one unit apart and the recommendation is not listed; exactly one apart and it stays, with a lower score.

The list is already filtered to what fits. A 1-unit lab is offered 1- and 2-hour recommendations; the 3-hour ones are gone. Courses with no units in COCI are not filtered — an absent measurement must not read as a failed one.

Mix and match freely. A course can take several recommendations, and one recommendation can serve several courses. Pick as many as fit — the card keeps a running total of chosen hours against the course's units, and a recommendation already used elsewhere just says so.

Small courses get their own shortlist. Confidence rewards how widely a recommendation is held, and the widely-held ones are the 3-hour ones — so a 1- or 2-unit course's best-fitting option sinks. Every card now also lists the recommendations whose hours equal its units, marked fits your units, even when they rank below the top five. That surfaced options on 12 courses that were previously invisible, 5 of them at 1–2 units.

Every number on this page opens the names behind it. Hover, tap or tab to a count — colleges, peer articulations, training records — and it lists them.

These are keyed to the credit recommendation, never to an MOS or rate. A service member can hold several MOSs, so the recommendation printed on the JST is the awardable unit — and each one lists the JST exhibits that carry it.

Where this comes from. Credit recommendations, ACE exhibits and peer articulations are read from the MAP platform's own credit records. Units, C-ID and control numbers come from COCI. Course list supplied by LATTC, 2026-08-27.

What this is not. Not an articulation and not an approval — a starting point for the discipline faculty who sign one. Choosing here records a decision; it does not create anything in MAP.
